You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Atlantic Coast Pipeline, LLC joint-venture interest, realized ~3-5-year record

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at ~2017-2019, the
> 3-5-year horizon after the ~2014 closing; facts are drawn from the in-window annual
> report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status in the outcome window (feasibility-relevant)
- The registrant remained a public reporting company through the outcome window: Piedmont
  Natural Gas Company, Inc. (Commission file 1-6196) appears as a named co-registrant on the
  combined annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal period ended December 31, 2019, filed
  jointly with Duke Energy Corporation and other Duke registrants, so an in-window public
  record for the relevant business exists. [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K cover]
- The realized trajectory of the joint venture is separately disclosed within that filing
  through the "Atlantic Coast Pipeline, LLC" regulatory-matters discussion and the Gas
  Utilities and Infrastructure segment; the outcome facts below are taken from those
  dedicated disclosures rather than inferred from consolidated results.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]

## Realized record of the acquired membership interest
- The originally acquired interest was reassigned after closing: per the filing's exhibit
  index, membership interests were assigned under an Assignment of Membership Interests dated
  October 3, 2016 between Piedmont ACP Company, LLC and Dominion Atlantic Coast Pipeline, LLC
  (incorporated by reference to a registrant Form 8-K filed October 7, 2016, File No. 1-06196).
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K exhibit index, item 10.5]
- By December 31, 2019 the disclosed ownership of ACP was Dominion 48%, Duke Energy 47%, and
  Southern Company Gas 5%; the registrant no longer appears among ACP's equity members and is
  described only as a prospective customer of the pipeline (with Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke
  Energy Progress and the registrant to purchase under 20-year supply contracts subject to
  state regulatory approval). [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]

## Realized record of the joint-venture project (best-documented scalars)
- Project cost: as of the FY2019 report, total project cost was approximately $8 billion,
  excluding financing costs, with the filing attributing the increase to delays resulting from
  legal challenges. [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]
- Schedule: as of the FY2019 report the project expected mechanical completion in late 2021
  with in-service likely in the first half of 2022.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]
- Operating/permitting disruption: the project was the subject of challenges in state and
  federal courts and agencies (including its biological opinion and incidental take statement,
  and crossings of the Blue Ridge Parkway, the Appalachian Trail, and the Monongahela and
  George Washington national forests), and a pending FERC Notice to Proceed for full
  construction in Virginia was held up by legal challenges as of the report date.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]
- Impairment assessment: at December 31, 2019 the carrying value of Duke Energy's equity
  method investment in ACP was $1.2 billion; following several adverse court rulings the
  investment was evaluated for impairment using probability-weighted discounted-cash-flow
  scenarios, and management concluded fair value approximated carrying value and the
  investment was not impaired as of that date.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable within the fixed window
- The pipeline was ultimately cancelled by its sponsors after the outcome window (July 2020),
  a development outside the fixed ~2017-2019 horizon and not sourced from an in-window primary
  filing here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the fixed ~2017-2019 window the joint venture's realized record, as separately
  disclosed by the acquirer, shows the registrant's original stake reassigned (October 2016;
  registrant not among the year-end 2019 members), the project's total cost reported at about
  $8 billion, its expected in-service reported as the first half of 2022, and an equity
  investment (Duke's 47%, $1.2 billion carrying value) evaluated for impairment after
  adverse court rulings but held at carrying value as of December 31, 2019.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001326160-20-000034, Form 10-K, Regulatory Matters]

[SLICE END]
